4.6 Special Regularisation Scheme

After the formation of this Government,

3,299 free House Site pattas/ e-pattas have been

issued to eligible families by regularizing the

residential encroachments of people who have

been residing for long period on unobjectionable

Government poramboke lands.

4.7 Land Administration -Simplification and Digitisation

In order to ensure better follow-up and

timely action on every application relating to land

transfer, land alienation and land exchange, an

integrated online system will be developed

covering the entire process from receipt of

application to issue of final orders.

141

All Tahsildars, District Revenue Officers and

District Collectors will be brought into the portal.

Reports and recommendations required at

different stages will also be obtained through the

portal. This will enable the Commissionarate to

closely monitor the movement of each application,

identify the level at which it is pending and ensure

timely action.

The system will provide for timelines at

important stages, along with reminders for

pending cases. This will help to reduce delays and

ensure that applications are not held up for want

of reports or follow-up.

219

7.19 Revenue Follow-up Work in

Corporations and Municipal Towns

The Government have ordered for the

commencement of Revenue follow up Work in all

the Municipalities and the Corporations of the

State (except Chennai old city) in order to update

the registries in Revenue Records, to issue pattas

to land holders and to prepare and hand over the

land records to District Revenue Administration

for maintenance as per G.O.(1D) No. 103,

Revenue Department, dated 01.03.2007. Now,

the work is in progress in 9 Corporations and

1 Municipality (Tenkasi). 26,41,975 pattas have

been issued so far since the year 2008 – 2009.

Abolition Acts and Ground Rent registers were

taken up for the grant of house-site pattas to

13,021 sub-divisions and 4,846 pattas have been

issued so far.

3.8.3. Patta for Industrial plots

41 Government Industrial Estates and

100 TANSIDCO owned Industrial Estates

were formed through transfer of land /

alienation from Government and other ways.

The classifications of these lands are

recorded in the revenue records as Sarkar

Poromboke in most Industrial Estates and as

Ryotwari in a few Industrial Estates. Hence,

MSMEs could not get the patta for these

lands.

To address this issue, the Government

formed an empowered committee headed by

the Chief Secretary to change the

classification of the land from Sarkar

Poramboke to Ryotwari lands. As a result,

the Government issued order for change the

classification of 2053 acres of Government

patta for their Industrial Plots.

6. Every worker shall have an opportunity of being heard and register any grievance either orally or in writing, at all implementation levels for disposal as per the provisions of the Grievance Redressal Mechanism under the Scheme.

17. Issuance of Rural Employment Guarantee Card in Case of Dislocation

1. Notwithstanding anything contained in this Schedule, in the event of any national calamity such as flood, cyclone, tsunami and earthquake resulting in mass dislocation of rural population, the adult members of rural households of areas so affected may—

a. Seek for registration and get Rural Employment Guarantee Card issued by the Village Panchayat or Block Development Officer (VP) of the area of temporary relocation;

b. Submit written or oral applications for work to the Block Development Officer (VP) or the Village Panchayat of the area of temporary relocation; and

c. Apply for re-registration and re-issuance of Rural Employment Guarantee Card in the event of any loss or

destruction.

2. The details of such Rural Employment Guarantee Card shall be intimated to the District Collector.

3. In the event of restoration of normalcy, the Rural Employment Guarantee Card so issued shall be re-endorsed at original place of habitation and clubbed with the original Rural Employment Guarantee Card on being retrieved.

4.The number of days of employment provided shall be counted while

computing 125 days of guaranteed employment per household.

CHAPTER-VII— DEMAND FOR WORK AND ALLOTMENT 18. Demand for Work

1. Every adult member of a registered household whose name appears in the Rural Employment Guarantee Card, shall be entitled to apply for unskilled manual work under the Scheme; and every

18

such application shall be compulsorily registered, and a receipt issued

with the date, which shall be entered in the given digital platform.

2, The District Administration shall proactively verify the requirements of the Vulnerable Groups and provide them with work.

3. Application for work may be oral or written and made to the Village Panchayat or to the Block Development Officer (VP) or through any other means authorized by the Government.
